method.audio: Authorized low-bandwidth YouTube audio collected with yt-dlp.
method.review: Full chronological ASR review by research agents; the main agent independently spot-checked procedure-bearing time windows against raw ASR.
method.evidence_boundary: Paraphrases preserve speaker or commentator scope. Static frame evidence can verify only visible sampled states, not movement, edit causality, sound, lens values or creator intent.

items.title: Depth of Field Explained: Ultimate Guide to Camera Focus [Shot List Ep. 4]

claims.uncertainty: Static examples show appearance, not lens settings.

claims.paraphrase: Deep focus can allow scanning and simultaneous action across several planes.
claims.uncertainty: Actual attention order must be tested with viewers.

claims.paraphrase: Shallow focus retains one sharp plane while foreground or background softens.
claims.uncertainty: No universal depth threshold.

claims.paraphrase: Shallow depth can isolate a subject and turn out-of-focus point lights into visible bokeh.

claims.paraphrase: The video interprets shallow focus and point of view as amplifying emotional pressure in Moonlight.
claims.uncertainty: Emotional causality is commentary.

claims.paraphrase: Soft focus leaves no region fully crisp and may sustain dream, flashback or unreal atmosphere.
claims.uncertainty: A style choice; accidental defocus can look similar.

claims.paraphrase: Rack focus transfers a shallow focus plane between subjects within one shot and guides attention without a cut.
claims.uncertainty: Static frames prove only endpoints, not the transition.

claims.paraphrase: The Host example uses a fast focus return that the commentary associates with shock and panic.
claims.uncertainty: Speed and emotional effect require clip evidence.

claims.paraphrase: A split diopter can render near and far zones sharp while leaving an intermediate seam or soft region.

claims.paraphrase: Tilt-shift focus can create a narrow sharp band and a miniature-like appearance.

items.title: Roger Deakins on "Learning to Light" — Cinematography Techniques Ep. 1

claims.uncertainty: First-person aesthetic judgment.

claims.paraphrase: He recalls using color and light relationships to create melancholy in a specific domestic setting.
claims.uncertainty: Project example, not a transferable palette recipe.

claims.paraphrase: Exposure judgment includes deciding what may fall toward black while keeping useful detail and preventing hotspots from becoming unusable.
claims.uncertainty: Tolerance depends on narrative and delivery medium.

claims.paraphrase: He recommends an overall reading and visual judgment rather than measuring every local variation.
claims.uncertainty: Experienced workflow, not permission to skip critical range checks.

claims.paraphrase: A quoted James Wong Howe anecdote frames simplicity as reducing lighting to one significant, pure dominant idea.

claims.paraphrase: When the overall light decision is wrong, Deakins favors admitting it and restarting instead of adding patches.
claims.uncertainty: First-person workflow; requires a comparable alternative.

claims.paraphrase: A small selected image can sometimes communicate more than an all-inclusive wide view.
claims.uncertainty: Not appropriate when spatial geography is the story purpose.

claims.paraphrase: Evaluate light by its visible direction, softness and contrast on faces and objects.
claims.uncertainty: Result-oriented principle, not a fixture instruction.

claims.paraphrase: Differences in light and color, or black and white, contribute to a cinematographer's individual way of seeing.
claims.uncertainty: Do not convert another cinematographer's signature into a style-copying template.

claims.paraphrase: Learning light depends on noticing subtle real-world changes and building a visual vocabulary through experience.
claims.uncertainty: Training advice; does not prove numerical camera settings.
